bullets.title: Netflix plunges ~9% on weak Q3 guidance and FCF miss
bullets.body: NFLX fell 7.7%-9.5% after-hours after Q2 came in roughly in-line (EPS $0.80 vs $0.79 est, rev $12.56B vs $12.58B) but Q3 guidance missed across the board: EPS $0.82 vs $0.84 est, revenue $12.86B vs $13.0B, and Q3 op margin 33.2% vs 33.5% est. The standout miss was FCF at $1.53B, -33% y/y versus the $2.72B consensus. Management blamed Olympics and World Cup timing; fintwit focused on content drought as the root cause. One account's Momentum Tracker had a SELL signal pre-print.

bullets.title: AAPL hits all-time high; HSBC upgrades to Buy with $366 PT
bullets.body: HSBC raised Apple to Buy from Hold with a price target of $366 (from $260), implying ~41% upside. AAPL was one of the few names hitting new 52-week (and all-time) highs on the day, up 0.6% premarket. One fintwit account described a simple dip-buy / breakout-sell approach to the stock.

bullets.title: Semis approaching bear-market territory; chip selloff weighs broadly
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks fell ~4.3% on the session and are now down ~19% from the June all-time high, nearing the conventional -20% bear-market threshold. Fintwit attributed the move to concern that AI infrastructure spending may not justify current valuations, amplified by Kimi K3's competitive release. One account noted the 2× DRAM ETF was down 17% on the day while one closely-watched name fell 24%.

bullets.title: GOOGL erases $200B market cap; Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed months
bullets.body: Alphabet closed down 4.4% on Thursday, wiping roughly $200B in market cap, after Bloomberg reported Gemini 3.5 Pro is months behind schedule due to insufficient coding capability improvements and internal review bottlenecks. Engineers reportedly frustrated about losing ground to Anthropic and OpenAI; one fintwit account cited internal capacity constraints as a further headwind.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 futures extend losses to 2%; S&P 500 futures -1.1% in Asia
bullets.body: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 2% and S&P 500 futures extended losses to 1.1% in overnight Asian trading, driven by the AI/chip selloff, NFLX earnings, and geopolitical escalation. The Nikkei fell as much as 6% and entered technical correction territory (>10% from June highs), Taiwan shares slid 6%, and the Kospi (closed for Constitution Day) saw 1.2M retail margin calls — 3.4% of Korea's adult population.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 profit +77% YoY; commits additional $100B to US; Taiwan shares -3.8%
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 2026 revenue of $40.2B (up 33.7% YoY, top of guidance) with gross margin of 67.7%, beating the guided 65.5%-67.5% range. The company committed an additional $100B to US manufacturing. Despite the beat, Taiwan-listed shares fell 3.8% in early trading as the broader chip trade reversed. D.A. Davidson raised its PT to $500 from $450; one fintwit account noted TSM bucked the typical post-earnings sell-the-news pattern and closed higher on the day.

bullets.title: Kimi K3 shakes AI competitive landscape; NVDA moat risk flagged
bullets.body: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 — a 2.8T-parameter MoE model with a 1M token context window — is ranking #2 on global benchmarks and reportedly closing the capability gap with US closed-source frontier models to under three months. A widely-cited tweet noted Jensen Huang himself warned that Chinese AI models may specialize toward Huawei chips, raising a structural risk to NVDA's long-term moat. One account argued Kimi K3 is net positive for hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL) as the AI value chain's orchestration layer.

bullets.title: Meta poaching top Amazon cloud exec amid cloud-push plans
bullets.body: Meta is hiring Dave Brown, a senior AWS computing executive, as the company weighs entering cloud services, per WSJ. Separately, Satya Nadella reportedly criticized Anthropic's 'Fable' content restrictions in an internal staff meeting, calling them senseless as Microsoft advances its own AI model strategy.

bullets.title: NBIS flagged as needing a bottom before neocloud sector bounces; Cramer also cautious
bullets.body: One fintwit trader described NBIS as 'still weak' and said the stock needs to find a low before the broader neocloud sector can bounce. Cramer on CNBC called Nebius 'very good company' but said the stock 'is not done going down' and current levels are not a good entry. One tracked account sold their position at $75.

bullets.title: ORCL down 64% from Sep 2025 peak; $600B market cap erased
bullets.body: Oracle has now fallen 64% since its September 2025 all-time high, a total market capitalization loss of approximately $600 billion. Separately, a regulatory obstacle emerged: New Mexico's Commissioner of Public Lands rejected a natural gas pipeline proposal for Project Jupiter, a large data center project tied to both ORCL and BE.

bullets.title: Jefferies bullish AMD ahead of Advancing AI 2026 event; expects MSFT and Anthropic MI400 wins
bullets.body: Jefferies issued a positive note on AMD ahead of its Advancing AI 2026 event next week, expecting announcements of new MI400 series wins with Microsoft and Anthropic as a positive catalyst. One account's infrastructure model currently incorporates AMD and custom ASICs alongside NVDA alternatives.

bullets.title: UBS DRAM cycle outlook: undersupplied until mid-2028; Micron Idaho fab mid-2027
bullets.body: One fintwit account cited a UBS semiconductor industry model projecting 2027 revenue of $1,760B with DRAM undersupply persisting until mid-2028. Micron's Idaho facility is expected online mid-2027; Samsung HBM fab ramps in H2 2027. Memory as a percentage of hyperscaler capex projected at 48% (per CLSA). The Meritz Securities analyst Kim Sunwoo argued markets are 'excessively misunderstanding' the semiconductor situation and DRAM shortage will intensify in H2 2026.

bullets.title: Broadcom invests $400M in Singapore chip packaging JV with Powertech
bullets.body: Broadcom and Taiwan's Powertech Technology are investing $400M in a joint venture plant in Singapore focused on high-end Fan-Out Panel-Level-Packaging (FOPLP) substrates for large AI chips. This adds to the growing capex buildout in advanced packaging for AI accelerators.

bullets.title: SNDK/MU seen moving together on DRAM correlation; LITE gaining photonics interest
bullets.body: One fintwit trader expects SNDK to trade in line with MU and the broader DRAM sector and is watching for entry points. Separately, a photonics-focused account flagged renewed interest in the sector ahead of earnings, tracking LITE, COHR, and AAOI. Another account said LITE is 'attractive after recent price decline.'

bullets.title: Global AI trade reversal hits Asian markets; Japan AI deleverage sends Kioxia -16%
bullets.body: FT reported 'global stocks tumble as AI trade goes into reverse.' Japanese stocks entered technical correction (Nikkei -5-6%, Topix -3%+) with semiconductor deleverage sending Kioxia down 16% from its June peak (market value now halved). Hong Kong AI stocks fell ~5% and Taiwan's tech benchmark fell ~5%. Foreign investors sold a record $5.8B in Taiwan shares.

bullets.title: GEV breaks below 50-day MA; technical signal flags potential -14% drop
bullets.body: GE Vernova closed below its 50-day moving average. The last time GEV lost this level, it declined 14% over the following two weeks, according to one fintwit account tracking chart patterns.

bullets.title: Fed's Jefferson: AI timing critical for inflation; current stance well-positioned
bullets.body: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson flagged AI as a key variable: if AI demand outpaces productivity gains, it could lift inflation; if productivity comes first, it eases price pressures. Jefferson said the labor market is stabilizing in a 'low-hire, low-fire' environment partly due to AI uncertainty. He warned the Fed may need to reconsider its stance if inflation fails to resume declining. Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan separately signaled openness to higher rates.

bullets.title: Single-stock vol vs. index vol spread hits dot-com bubble levels
bullets.body: One widely-circulated chart (sourced to Goldman Sachs) showed single-stock volatility relative to index volatility at its highest level since the dot-com bubble. BofA quants separately warned that the stock/index vol spread approaching these extremes signals elevated 'shock risk.'

bullets.title: GOOGL workers rally at Mountain View HQ over layoff concerns
bullets.body: Google employees staged a rally at the company's Mountain View headquarters organized by the Alphabet Workers Union, calling for voluntary exits and severance guarantees amid ongoing job security concerns related to layoffs. No production halt or work stoppage reported.

bullets.title: Verizon to sell 274 stores and cut 500 corporate jobs
bullets.body: Verizon announced it will sell 274 retail stores and lay off an additional 500 corporate employees as part of a cost restructuring initiative, signaling continued margin pressure in the US wireless carrier market.
